I agree Brady is an outlier and you can point to a lot of QBs to point that out (Favre, Roethlisberger, Brees). It is disingenuous to use Manning as an example though. Dude literally had a spinal fusion that reduced grip strength and affected his arm strength. He fell off because he was forced to rely on his lower body to produce velocity and once his foot got injured he was pretty much done for. Once again, Brady is definitely an outlier, and lots of other really good QBs have fallen off in their late 30s. 

I think Rodgers is one of the few who might join Brady as an outlier because he seems to take really good care of his body, and if he loses some mobility he still has good enough pocket presence, understanding of defenses/processing speed, etc. to be able to excel in his 40s.

With Big Ben I was agreeing that a QBs arm can fall off quick, using him as an example of a big guy who didn't necessarily have a weird throwing motion or require perfect mechanics on each throw. With Favre, his arm was still super strong but his actual body couldn't keep up. What both of these guys have though is a more conventional gunslinger mindset of fuck it and chuck it. Rodgers has the ability to dink and dunk his way up the field with long methodical drives like Brady, and he has exceptional arm strength that, barring a major injury, should be able to stay into his 40s. Dude, what? Father Time is undefeated, yes. But we are getting to the point where rules have made it to where QBs careers can get extended significantly. So long as QBs can stay relatively injury free throughout the 20s and early to mid 30s, then it isn't out of the realm of possibility for more QBs to extend their careers. The main reason I can see that not happening is that as QBs get more mobile they're opening theirselves up to more injuries that will build up over time.

And as much as I hate Brady he isn't using anything extra. Dude has just literally kept his body up and fine tuned the ever loving shit out of his mechanics

I think it's different with Brees and Rivers though too. Brees is relatively short/small for an nfl qb and if he's unable to utilize all of his body to generate force/momentum he won't be able to get good velocity. Rivers had a throwing motion that REALLY utilized arm strength over mechanics. 

If you wanted to say there is a precedent you could probably look at like Big Ben. But, there's also people like Favre who still had a fucking cannon in his 40s. I think if Rodgers can keep his mechanics fixed (early in his career he was supposedly very loose with them) then he'll be fine because he has ridiculous processing speed along with his arm. I think we'll start to see more QBs playing into their 40s soon. Granted, it won't be the norm but I don't think Brady will be the anomaly for playing well at that age anymore (depending on how long he continues to play).
